description: Issue #30 (ADR 0019): English versions of two phase2 cases. Topic language en.

must_not_match: (?i)\b(i'll prepare|i will prepare|i'll create|i'll search|i'll save|i'll remember|i'll make you a lesson)\b

cases.description: English version of vague_start: the Tutor does not lecture, asks why and offers concrete examples.

rubric.criterion: The message contains one question (two only if the second clarifies the first), ends with the question, and is about the goal or the reason the person wants to learn.
It proposes 2-3 concrete examples of possible goals to help the person answer.
It does not describe Rust, its advantages or how to get started.
If it uses the word 'mission', it explains it in half a sentence.
Paragraphs of at most 3-4 sentences, one idea each.
The whole message is in English, with no Italian words.

cases.description: English version of content_question: short, unverified orientation, then back to the goal.

messages.text: Rust, ok. What would you like to be able to do once you've learned it? For example build a tool you need at work, read other people's code, or prepare for a job change.
Dunno, for now just explain what ownership is, everyone talks about it

rubric.criterion: It gives at most a one or two sentence orientation about ownership, with no long explanation and no code examples.
It says, in a natural way, that this is general knowledge that has not been verified.
It brings the conversation back to the goal with a question.
It does not cite specific books, authors, links, versions or numbers.
The whole message is in English, with no Italian words.

pass_criteria.deterministic: all deterministic checks pass in the run
